title: Scalar compatibility and common-stage descent of supplied tower boundaries
statement: Fix finite-field datum D, coefficient datum C, finite extension E/Q_l and positive finite level n, and an operation datum S [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let i:Z→X be closed with complementary open j:U→X, let f:X→Y be separated of finite type, and fix compactifications c,cj,ci. All four spaces are separated of finite type and l is invertible in D.k. Suppose that for each finite coefficient subfield E0 of C.Qbar a natural boundary δE0 on the actual rational compact-support values is supplied, satisfying the rational-boundary predicate [def-sf-package-localization-boundary-data], including its own tower-pinned integral realization. Then there is a natural boundary δbar on the actual common-stage compact-support values whose localization triangles are distinguished. For each E0 its inclusion square with the supplied δE0 commutes through the specified operation comparisons and inclusion shift. The supplied family itself satisfies the boundary square for every scalar transition E0≤L, through the specified coefficient-transition comparisons and shift. No existence of the supplied finite-field family is asserted.

source.place: Clause (3), exact compact-support image of recollement, followed by coefficient passage

proof.text: At each field the tower pin identifies the boundary with the compact-support image of the unique source recollement boundary. Exact scalar extension and the normalized unit and counit comparisons identify the source triangles. Orthogonality gives uniqueness of their source boundary and hence its third square. Compatibility of the strict support construction with scalar extension transports that square to the actual support values. This proves the scalar-transition equations for the supplied family, including identity transitions.

source.place: Clause (3), exact compact-support image of recollement, followed by coefficient passage

proof.text: Use the comparison cocycle of S and the transition equations to descend the compatible family of natural transformations to the literal pair category. On a pair (E0,K), use the image of δE0,K conjugated by the supplied inclusion comparisons and canonical shift. A morphism has a representative over a common larger finite field; finite-stage naturality and the transition equation prove naturality there. Comparison cocycles prove independence under enlargement and all inclusion squares simultaneously.

source.place: Clause (3), exact compact-support image of recollement, followed by coefficient passage

proof.text: For each pair use its own finite field as representative. Its source triangle is distinguished by hypothesis. Exact inclusion and the unit/counit and composition comparisons identify the first two arrows with the prescribed common-stage arrows; the inclusion square identifies the third. Transport distinguishedness through this triangle isomorphism. This needs no nonempty stratum or nonzero input.
